instruction:
# Apply the east warehouse cycle count

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

The east warehouse was counted on 2026-09-13. The count sheet is `/app/counts/east-2026-09-13.csv`, with one row per counted shelf: the item's sku, the quantity counted, and when that shelf was counted (UTC). Bring the system in line with the count:

- Some rows name a sku that does not exist. Write those skus to `/app/count-exceptions.txt`, one per line, and do not record anything for them.

description: Services: record damage reports from tickets as stock adjustments, answer and resolve them
instruction:
# Process the damage reports

The warehouse team reports damaged goods as tickets in the `tickets` service. Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service. You can use both through the `tickets` and `inventory` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `damage` is a report that names a sku, a warehouse and a number of damaged units. Its damage is recorded in inventory as adjustments with reason `damage` and reference `TCK-<ticket id>`, taken from that item in that warehouse. A report is recorded when the `damage` adjustments under its reference add up to minus its damaged units. Colleagues recorded some reports before you without answering the tickets, not always correctly.

Process the reports one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first. For each report:

- If it is already recorded, record nothing. Add one comment to the ticket that contains the id of the existing adjustment (for example `adj-123`), and set the ticket to `resolved`.
- Otherwise record the difference with one `adjust_stock` call: the units still missing so that the `damage` adjustments under its reference add up to minus its damaged units, reason `damage`, reference `TCK-<ticket id>`. Then add one comment that contains the id of the adjustment you just recorded, and set the ticket to `resolved`.
- If the warehouse does not hold enough units of the item to take out that difference, given the stock left after the reports before it, record nothing, add one comment that says `insufficient stock`, and set the ticket to `pending`.

Add exactly one comment to each ticket you process. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

The repository in `/app` holds `shipclient`, our HTTP client library. The error catalog for our services is published in the `docs` service, which you can use through the `docs` MCP server.

`/app/shipclient/errors.py` maps error codes to their HTTP status, whether the error is retryable, and its message, but it holds only a few codes and some of them are out of date. Make `ERRORS` match the current error catalog: every code the catalog defines, with the status, retryable flag and message it gives now, and nothing else. Deprecated codes that the catalog says to map to another code must be present too, with the entry of the code they map to. Messages must match the catalog exactly.

Keep `ErrorInfo`, `ERRORS` and `describe` as they are, and use the Python standard library only. `/app/tests` has a few tests you can run with `cd /app && python -m unittest`; your table will also be checked against the full catalog.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: open one follow-up ticket per component affected by an incident
instruction:
# Open follow-up tickets for incident INC-2291

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

The ticket for incident INC-2291 lists the components the incident affected. Open one follow-up ticket for each affected component:

- title: `Follow-up INC-2291: <component>`
- team: the team that owns the component, as listed in the current component ownership table, which is kept in a ticket labeled `ownership`
- priority: `P2`
- labels: `followup`
- body: one sentence saying what should be reviewed for that component

There must be exactly one follow-up ticket per affected component. Then add one comment to the incident ticket that lists the ids of the follow-up tickets as `#<id>`, and set the incident ticket to status `resolved`. Do not change any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: deploy a hotfix to the production environments that lack it, per release branch
instruction:
# Roll out hotfix HF-2291

Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service, which you can use through the `deploy` MCP server.

The advisory is `/app/hotfix/HF-2291.md`, and the changelog of each release branch is in `/app/hotfix/changelog/`. Every live commit is on exactly one release branch, and environments of the same service can run different branches.

The production environments are `prod` and `prod-eu`; `staging` is out of scope. For every production environment of every service the `deploy` service lists, classify its live release and act on it:

1. `not_affected`: the service is not in the advisory's list of affected services, or the live commit is on a branch the advisory does not list as affected. Leave it alone.
2. `already_fixed`: the live commit has the fix. A commit has the fix when, in its branch's changelog, the newest `HF-2291` entry at or below it (the commit itself or an older one) applies the fix rather than reverting it. Leave it alone.
3. Otherwise build the advisory's commit for the live commit's branch, for that service. If the build fails, the environment is `build_failed`: do not deploy anything else in its place. If it succeeds, deploy it to that environment; it is `deployed`.

Do not move an environment to another branch, do not roll anything back, and do not touch `staging`. Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/hotfix-report.json` as:

```json
{"deployed": {"<service>@<environment>": "<commit now live>", ...}, "already_fixed": [...], "not_affected": [...], "build_failed": [...]}
```

Every production environment appears exactly once, as `<service>@<environment>`; the three lists are in alphabetical order.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: roll back degraded production releases one step at a time within a window
instruction:
# Roll back the degraded production releases

Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service, which you can use through the `deploy` MCP server.

A bad deployment wave early on 2026-09-14 left several services degraded in `prod`. For every service whose live `prod` release is not `healthy`:

- Roll `prod` back, one `rollback` call at a time, until the live release is `healthy`. A rollback returns to the release that the live one replaced, which `status` shows as `previous_release_id`. Some services need more than one rollback.
- Never roll back to a release created before 2026-09-10T00:00:00Z. If the next rollback would do that, or there is no release to return to, stop and leave that service where it is.
- Each `rollback` call creates a new release and moves one step back, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Only `prod` is in scope. Do not deploy anything and do not touch `staging`.

Write `/app/rollback-report.json` as `{"rolled_back": {"<service>": "<commit now live in prod>", ...}, "needs_attention": [...]}`. `rolled_back` has an entry for every service you rolled back at least once. `needs_attention` lists, in alphabetical order, the services still not healthy in `prod` when you stopped.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: quarantine the lots a supplier recall covers, across bins, sites and an old item code, after a colleague's partial work
instruction:
# Quarantine the lots under recall RC-2611

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

A supplier has recalled lots of two of its parts under recall RC-2611. Its notice of 2026-09-10 and the amendment of 2026-09-12 are in `/app/recall/`, together with `part-map.csv`, which maps the supplier's part numbers to our item codes.

How stock is kept:

- Each lot is its own item. Its sku is the item code followed by the lot (for example `HP-4471-L26213-2` is lot 26213-2 of item code HP-4471), and its name gives the lot.
- Stock is held per storage location. The service calls locations warehouses: pass a location name wherever a tool takes `warehouse`. Locations are named `<site>-<bin>`, at three sites, `east`, `west` and `north`, and each site has a quarantine location `<site>-Q`.

What to do:

1. A lot is affected when the notice, as amended, covers it. Where the amendment and the notice differ, the amendment holds.
2. Quarantine every unit of an affected lot that is on hand outside a quarantine location: move it to the quarantine location of the same site. Record each move as two `adjust_stock` calls with reason `transfer` and reference `RC-2611`: the quantity taken out of the location it is in, and the same quantity added to `<site>-Q`.
3. A colleague started on 2026-09-11, working from the notice before the amendment came, and stopped partway. Their moves also use the reference `RC-2611`. Leave the moves that are right as they are. Where a move took units out of a location and never added them to the quarantine location, add them there. Where a move quarantined a lot that is not affected, move those units back to the location they came from, recorded the same way (out of `<site>-Q`, into that location).
4. Write `/app/RC-2611.csv`, a CSV file with the header `sku,quarantined,shipped` and one row per affected lot in the inventory, including lots with nothing left on hand. `quarantined` is the number of units of the lot in quarantine locations when you are done. `shipped` is the number of units of the lot shipped to customers: minus the sum of the lot's adjustments with reason `shipment`.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service and code: move an API list client to the cursor pagination and rate limit contract in the docs, among a superseded revision and a draft
instruction:
# Update the Tidewater list client

The repository in `/app` holds `freight`, our integration with Tidewater, our freight carrier. `list_all` in `/app/freight/tidewater.py` still follows an old revision of Tidewater's API and no longer works against it. Tidewater's API reference is mirrored in the `docs` service, which you can use through the `docs` MCP server.

Update `list_all` to the contract in force for Tidewater's list endpoints: paths, pagination, page size, filters, the end of a listing, rate limits and errors. The docs service also holds a superseded revision and a draft; follow the pages in force.

Keep the function's signature and docstring contract, `Response`, `Transport` and `ApiError`, and use the Python standard library only. Every wait must go through the `sleep` argument and every reading of the clock through `now`. `/app/tests` has a test you can run with `cd /app && python -m unittest`. The client will also be checked against a server that behaves as Tidewater's reference describes: it must return every item of the listing once and in order, send only the requests the contract calls for, with the parameters it requires, and wait exactly as long as the contract says.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;

description: Service: build, stage, check and promote a release plan with non-idempotent deploys
instruction:
# Ship the 2026-09-14 release plan

Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service, which you can use through the `deploy` MCP server.

The release plan is `/app/release/plan.csv`: one row per service with the commit to ship and a `hold` flag. Work through every row whose `hold` is `no`; leave held services alone.

1. Build the commit. If the build fails, do not deploy it; the service is `failed_build`.
2. Deploy the build to `staging`, unless that build is already the live release in `staging`.
3. Check the health of the live `staging` release. If it is not `healthy`, the service is `degraded`: do not promote it, and if you deployed it to staging in step 2, roll `staging` back once so it returns to the release it replaced. If someone else had already deployed it, leave staging as it is.
4. If it is healthy, deploy the same build to `prod`, unless it is already the live release in `prod`. The service is `promoted`.

Every `deploy` and every `rollback` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/release-report.json` as `{"promoted": [...], "failed_build": [...], "degraded": [...]}`, each list holding service names in alphabetical order.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: refill west stock from two sources with floors, after completing a half-done job
instruction:
# Refill the west warehouse

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

Several west shelves have run low. Refill them as follows.

1. A replenishment job ran at 06:00 UTC today and stopped partway. Some of its transfers, which use the reference `RP-0914-<sku>`, took stock out of `north` but never added it to `west`. For each of those, record the missing west side: the same quantity added to `west`, reason `transfer`, same reference. Apply step 2 to the quantities you get after this.
2. An item needs a refill when it is not discontinued, its category is `fasteners`, `hydraulics` or `electrical`, it is stocked in `west` (it has a `west` entry), and its west quantity is below its `reorder_point`. Bring its west quantity up to twice its `reorder_point`, taking from `north` first and then from `east`. A source warehouse never goes below the item's `reorder_point`, and a warehouse with no entry for the item has nothing to give.
3. Record every move as two `adjust_stock` calls with reason `transfer` and reference `RP-0914-<sku>`: the quantity taken out of the source warehouse, and the same quantity added to `west`.
4. When `north` and `east` together cannot cover a refill, move what they can and write the item to `/app/shortfall.csv`, a CSV file with the header `sku,missing` and one row per such item giving the quantity still missing.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: record a shipment feed against partial and wrong earlier records, without a write key
instruction:
# Record yesterday's shipments

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

The warehouse system exported the orders shipped on 2026-09-13 to `/app/shipments/2026-09-13.jsonl`, one order per line: the order id, the warehouse it shipped from, and its lines (sku and quantity). Staff recorded some of these shipments by hand during the day, not always correctly. Make the stock records match the export:

- A shipped line is recorded by `adjust_stock` adjustments with reason `shipment`, the order id as reference, and the order's warehouse. For every line, the adjustments for that order, sku and warehouse must add up to minus the shipped quantity.
- Where nothing was recorded for a line, record it. Where a line was recorded with the wrong quantity, record one more adjustment with the difference, so the total comes out right. Where it was recorded correctly, record nothing.
- The export repeats one order. An order that appears twice shipped once.
- Some lines cannot be recorded because the warehouse does not have the stock. Do not record those lines at all, and write them to `/app/blocked.csv`, a CSV file with the header `order,sku,missing` and one row per such line, where `missing` is the quantity that still needed to be recorded.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service: find the tickets that breached the support SLA, comment on each and file one report
instruction:
# Report support SLA breaches

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

The support SLA policy is kept in the open ticket labeled `sla-policy`. Apply it to every ticket it covers, measured up to now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC, and find the tickets that breached their first-response target, their resolution target, or both.

1. Add exactly one comment to each breached ticket, with the text `SLA breach: <metrics>`, where `<metrics>` is `first-response`, `resolution`, or `first-response, resolution`. A ticket that already has a comment starting with `SLA breach:` was reported by an earlier review: do not comment on it again.
2. Create one ticket that reports the review:
   - title: `SLA breach report 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P2`
   - labels: `sla-report`
   - body: one line per breached ticket, including those reported by an earlier review, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <metrics>`, and nothing else

Do not change the status or priority of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Services: decide warranty claims in tickets under a policy ticket, ship replacements from inventory, answer and set status
instruction:
# Process the warranty returns

Customers ask for warranty replacements through tickets in the `tickets` service. Products and stock are kept in the `inventory` service. You can use both through the `tickets` and `inventory` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `warranty` is a claim. The warranty policy is the open ticket labeled `warranty-policy`: it decides which claims are covered, what to ship and from which warehouse. A replacement is shipped with one `adjust_stock` call: the replacement sku, the warehouse, delta minus the claim's units, reason `shipment`, reference `RMA-<ticket id>`.

Colleagues shipped some replacements before you without answering the tickets. A claim whose reference already has a `shipment` adjustment has been shipped: ship nothing more, and answer it with that adjustment.

Two open claims for the same serial are one claim. The one with the higher ticket id is a duplicate of the other: answer it as a duplicate and do nothing else for it. This rule comes before every other.

Process the claims one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first, so that each one sees the stock the ones before it left. Add exactly one comment to each claim and set its status:

- Shipped, by you or before you: `Replacement <sku> shipped from <warehouse> as <adjustment id>.` with the sku and warehouse of the shipment and its adjustment id (for example `adj-123`). Status `resolved`.
- Not covered: `Not covered: <reason>.` with the reason the policy gives. Status `closed`.
- Covered, but no warehouse can ship it: `Backordered: <sku>.` Status `pending`.
- Duplicate: `Duplicate of #<ticket id of the other claim>.` Status `duplicate`.

Ship nothing for a claim that is not covered, backordered or a duplicate. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

description: Service and code: verify signed event requests per the provider docs, with key rotation, a clock skew window and a deprecated scheme
instruction:
# Verify signed payment events

The repository in `/app` holds `receiver`, the service that takes payment events from Corvid, our card processor. Corvid signs every request, and we do not check the signatures yet. Corvid's developer documentation is mirrored in the `docs` service, which you can use through the `docs` MCP server.

Implement `verify` in `/app/receiver/signature.py` so that it accepts exactly the requests that Corvid's current signature rules accept, and make `handle` in `/app/receiver/handler.py` follow those rules too. The docs service also describes an older signature scheme; follow the rules in force.

Keep the signatures and docstring contracts of `verify` and `handle`, and `EVENTS`, and use the Python standard library only. `/app/tests` has a few tests you can run with `cd /app && python -m unittest`. Both functions will also be checked against signed and tampered requests that those tests do not cover.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
